blocks.text: Imagine streaming a live concert online. What factors determine the quality and speed of your connection? Understanding network performance metrics is crucial for optimizing such experiences.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore key network performance metrics: bandwidth, latency, propagation delay, jitter, and throughput. These metrics help us understand and optimize network performance, crucial for applications like video streaming, online gaming, and cloud computing.

blocks.title: Bandwidth
blocks.text: Bandwidth is the maximum rate at which data can be transferred over a network path, typically measured in bits per second (bps).

blocks.title: Latency
blocks.text: Latency is the time it takes for a data packet to travel from the source to the destination, measured in milliseconds (ms).

blocks.title: Throughput
blocks.text: Throughput is the actual rate at which data is successfully transferred over a network, often less than the bandwidth due to network conditions.

blocks.markdown: To understand these metrics better, consider a highway analogy: bandwidth is like the number of lanes, latency is the time it takes to travel from one point to another, and throughput is the number of cars that successfully reach their destination per unit time.

blocks.title: Calculating Total Delay
blocks.prompt: Calculate the total delay for a data packet traveling through a network with a transmission delay of 10 ms, a propagation delay of 5 ms, and a queuing delay of 2 ms.

steps.text: Identify the given delays: transmission delay = 10 ms, propagation delay = 5 ms, queuing delay = 2 ms.
Sum the delays to find the total delay.

blocks.title: Bandwidth-Delay Product
blocks.text: The bandwidth-delay product is the amount of data that can be in transit in the network. It is calculated as the product of bandwidth and round-trip time (RTT).

blocks.title: Bandwidth-Delay Product
blocks.prompt: A network has a bandwidth of 100 Mbps and a round-trip time (RTT) of 50 ms. Calculate the bandwidth-delay product.

steps.text: Convert bandwidth to bits per second: 100 Mbps = 100,000,000 bps.
Convert RTT to seconds: 50 ms = 0.05 s.
